# `vb` command reference

<!-- Generated by `vb help --markdown`; do not edit. Regenerate: `vb help --markdown > docs/cli.md`. -->

`vb` manages and runs Voxel Browser (user-scoped, no admin rights). `vb help <command>` prints the same information for one command; `vb help --json` prints this whole table as JSON.

## Conventions for scripts and agents

- **Exit codes:** `0` success, `1` the operation failed, `2` bad command line.
- **Errors** go to stderr as `error: <what went wrong>`, followed by `hint: <what to do>` when one exists. Non-fatal notes are `warning: ...`.
- **`--json`** on every command that reports state (`list`, `which`, `paths`, `doctor`, `install`, `update`, `server list|status`, `structure validate`, `pack *`) prints one JSON document on stdout and nothing else.
- **No prompts.** Nothing asks a question; destructive actions refuse unless given `--yes` or `--force`.
- **Environment:** `VB_HOME=<dir>` keeps everything under one directory (portable/CI); `VB_SOURCE=<src>` selects the release source (`owner/repo[@base-url]` or `dir:/path`).

## Commands

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `vb completions <bash|zsh|fish|powershell>` | print a shell completion script |
| `vb docs [<topic>] [--path] [--version v]` | print the documentation shipped with a version |
| `vb doctor` | check paths, versions and configuration |
| `vb host [--version v] [--port n] [--pack dir] [--watch] [-- server args...]` | run a server in the foreground (Ctrl+C stops it) |
| `vb install [<version>] [--build debug] [--force]` | download, verify and install a release |
| `vb launch [--version <v>] [--connect host[:port]] [-- client args...]` | start the client |
| `vb link <name> <build-dir>` | register a local build as a pseudo-version |
| `vb list [--remote] [--json]` | show installed versions and links (* = default) |
| `vb pack <init|check|dev|types|info> ...` | create, validate and run a content pack |
| `vb paths [--json]` | print the data/config/cache directories |
| `vb prune [--keep N]` | remove old, non-default versions |
| `vb self update [--check] [--force]` | update vb itself to the latest release |
| `vb server <new|list|start|stop|restart|status|logs|config|service|rm> ...` | manage named, background server instances |
| `vb shim <install|remove>` | put voxel_browser / voxel_browser_server launchers in <data>/bin |
| `vb structure <new|edit|validate> ...` | author decorative structures (new, edit in the editor, validate) |
| `vb uninstall <version> [--force]` | remove an installed version (or a link) |
| `vb unlink <name> [--force]` | remove a link |
| `vb update` | install the latest release |
| `vb use <version>` | set the default version |
| `vb which [client|server|editor] [--version <v>] [--json]` | print a binary's path |

## `vb completions`

```
vb completions <bash|zsh|fish|powershell>

print a shell completion script

Prints a shell completion script generated from the same command table.

examples:
  vb completions bash > ~/.vb-completions    # bash
```

## `vb docs`

```
vb docs [<topic>] [--path] [--version v]

print the documentation shipped with a version

Prints the documentation that ships with the installed version, so an offline agent reads exactly the docs of the engine it targets. No topic lists them; a topic is a file name (`cli.md`, `lua-api.md`) or a Lua name such as `vb.world.raycast`.

options:
  --path                  print the docs directory
  --version <v>           which installed version

examples:
  vb docs vb.world.raycast    # the reference entry for one function
  vb docs --path    # where the docs are
```

## `vb doctor`

```
vb doctor

check paths, versions and configuration

Checks the platform, data directory, release source, installed versions and links, and the default version. Exit code 1 when a check fails.

options:
  --json                  print {ok, problems, checks:[{level,text}]}

examples:
  vb doctor --json    # machine-readable health check

Supports --json (machine-readable output).
```

## `vb host`

```
vb host [--version v] [--port n] [--pack dir] [--watch] [-- server args...]

run a server in the foreground (Ctrl+C stops it)

Runs a dedicated server in the foreground (Ctrl+C stops it). With `--watch` it restarts whenever the pack changes on disk. Everything after `--` goes to the server.

options:
  --version <v>           which installed version
  --port <n>              UDP port
  --pack <dir>            content pack directory (default: the bundled base pack); each pack keeps its own world
  --watch                 restart the server when files in the pack change

examples:
  vb host --pack ./my_pack --watch    # develop a pack with auto-restart
```

## `vb install`

```
vb install [<version>] [--build debug] [--force]

download, verify and install a release

Downloads a release, verifies its checksum (and signature when a trusted key is configured) and unpacks it under the data directory. The first installed version becomes the default. With no version, installs the latest release.

options:
  --force                 reinstall even if the version is already installed
  --build debug           install the debug build instead of the release build
  --json                  print {version, already_installed, default_set} instead of progress output

examples:
  vb install    # install the latest release
  vb install v0.6.0 --json    # install one version, machine-readable

Supports --json (machine-readable output).
```

## `vb launch`

```
vb launch [--version <v>] [--connect host[:port]] [-- client args...]

start the client

Starts the client of a version in the foreground with the user's shared settings and a per-user singleplayer world directory. Everything after `--` goes to the client.

options:
  --version <v>           which installed version
  --connect host[:port]   join a server instead of the main menu

examples:
  vb launch --connect localhost:7777    # join a local server
  vb launch -- --singleplayer    # start singleplayer directly
```

## `vb link`

```
vb link <name> <build-dir>

register a local build as a pseudo-version

Registers a local build directory as a pseudo-version so engine developers can run `vb host --version <name>` against it.

examples:
  vb link dev ./build    # use ./build as version "dev"
```

## `vb list`

```
vb list [--remote] [--json]

show installed versions and links (* = default)

Lists installed versions and links; `*` marks the default.

options:
  --remote                list the versions available to install instead
  --json                  print an array of {name, kind, default, path, exists}

examples:
  vb list --json    # installed versions as JSON

Supports --json (machine-readable output).
```

## `vb pack`

```
vb pack <init|check|dev|types|info> ...

create, validate and run a content pack

Create, validate and run a content pack. All subcommands are non-interactive; a pack is a directory with pack.toml, init.lua and optional blocks/, entities/, biomes/, ui/ and textures/.

`vb pack check` and `vb pack dev` choose the newest installed version that satisfies the pack's engine_version_req (or `--version`, which must satisfy it too); if none does they print the `vb install` to run.

Files in ui/ run in the client UI VM (`ui`, `client`); all others in the server VM (`vb`). `vb pack check` enforces that.

subcommands:
  vb pack init [dir] [--template minimal|ui|worldgen|base] [--name id] [--engine-req range] [--force] [--json]
      scaffold a pack (pack.toml, init.lua, README.md, AGENTS.md, .luarc.json, editor stubs)
  vb pack check [dir] [--json] [--strict] [--version v]
      load the pack headless and print file:line diagnostics
  vb pack dev [dir] [--version v] [--port n] [--no-client]
      host with restart on save and open the client
  vb pack types [dir] [--version v] [--force] [--json]
      (re)write .vb/lua stubs, .luarc.json and ui/.luarc.json
  vb pack info [dir] [--json]
      name, version, engine requirement, file counts

options:
  --json                  init/check/types/info: machine-readable output
  --force                 init: write into a non-empty directory; types: overwrite .luarc.json and ui/.luarc.json
  --template <t>          init: minimal (default), ui, worldgen, or base (a copy of the installed content/base)
  --name <id>             init: pack id, [a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,31} (default: the directory name)
  --engine-req <range>    init: engine_version_req to write (default ">=<selected version>")
  --strict                check: warnings fail the check too
  --version <v>           which installed version to use
  --port <n>              dev: server port (default 7777)
  --no-client             dev: only host, do not open the client

examples:
  vb pack init my_pack && cd my_pack    # scaffold a pack
  vb pack check --json    # validate; exit 0 clean, 1 errors
  vb pack dev    # host with auto-restart and open the client
  vb pack init --template base my_mod    # start from a copy of base

Supports --json (machine-readable output).
```

## `vb paths`

```
vb paths [--json]

print the data/config/cache directories

Prints the data, config and cache directories (`VB_HOME` relocates all three).

options:
  --json                  print {data, config, cache}

examples:
  vb paths --json

Supports --json (machine-readable output).
```

## `vb prune`

```
vb prune [--keep N]

remove old, non-default versions

Removes old, non-default releases and leftover staging directories. Versions that a server instance pins or runs from are kept.

options:
  --keep N                keep the newest N releases (default 2)

examples:
  vb prune --keep 1    # keep only the newest release
```

## `vb self`

```
vb self update [--check] [--force]

update vb itself to the latest release

Updates `vb` itself to the latest release.

subcommands:
  vb self update [--check] [--force]
      update vb itself

options:
  --check                 only report whether an update exists
  --force                 update even if up to date

examples:
  vb self update --check    # is there a newer vb
```

## `vb server`

```
vb server <new|list|start|stop|restart|status|logs|config|service|rm> ...

manage named, background server instances

Named, persistent server instances (each with its own server.toml, world, logs and pinned version) that run in the background.

subcommands:
  vb server new <name> [--version v] [--pack dir] [--port n]
      create an instance
  vb server list [--json]
      list instances
  vb server start <name>
      start in the background
  vb server stop <name>
      stop gracefully (saves the world)
  vb server restart <name>
      stop then start
  vb server status [<name>] [--json]
      uptime, players, port
  vb server logs <name> [-f] [-n N]
      show (and follow) the log
  vb server config <name> <get|set|unset|edit> ...
      read or change server.toml
  vb server service <name> <install|remove>
      run as an OS service
  vb server rm <name> [--keep-world] [--yes]
      delete an instance

options:
  --json                  on list/status: machine-readable output
  --yes                   on rm: also delete the saved world without refusing

examples:
  vb server new survival --pack ./my_pack    # create an instance
  vb server start survival    # start it detached
  vb server status --json    # all instances

Supports --json (machine-readable output).
```

## `vb shim`

```
vb shim <install|remove>

put voxel_browser / voxel_browser_server launchers in <data>/bin

Puts `voxel_browser` and `voxel_browser_server` launchers in <data>/bin that run the default version.

subcommands:
  vb shim install
      create the launchers
  vb shim remove
      delete them

examples:
  vb shim install    # create the launchers
```

## `vb structure`

```
vb structure <new|edit|validate> ...

author decorative structures (new, edit in the editor, validate)

Author decorative structures (trees, ruins) for a pack: scaffold a data file, edit it visually in the structure editor, validate it headless.

subcommands:
  vb structure new <name>
      scaffold structures/<name>.lua
  vb structure edit <file>
      open the structure editor
  vb structure validate [<pack>] [--json]
      check every structure of a pack

options:
  --json                  validate: machine-readable report

examples:
  vb structure new oak_tree    # scaffold a structure file

Supports --json (machine-readable output).
```

## `vb uninstall`

```
vb uninstall <version> [--force]

remove an installed version (or a link)

Removes an installed release (or just the link file for a link). Refused while a server instance depends on the version unless `--force`.

options:
  --force                 remove it even if instances depend on it

examples:
  vb uninstall v0.5.0    # remove one version
```

## `vb unlink`

```
vb unlink <name> [--force]

remove a link

Removes a link (never touches the linked build directory).

options:
  --force                 remove even if instances use it

examples:
  vb unlink dev    # forget the link named dev
```

## `vb update`

```
vb update

install the latest release

Installs the latest release next to the existing ones; `vb use` switches the default.

options:
  --json                  same as `vb install --json`

examples:
  vb update    # get the newest release

Supports --json (machine-readable output).
```

## `vb use`

```
vb use <version>

set the default version

Sets the default version used when a command is not given `--version`.

examples:
  vb use v0.6.0    # make v0.6.0 the default
```

## `vb which`

```
vb which [client|server|editor] [--version <v>] [--json]

print a binary's path

Prints the path of the client, server or editor binary of a version.

options:
  --version <v>           which installed version (default: the default)
  --json                  print {version, kind, path}

examples:
  vb which server --json    # where is the default server binary

Supports --json (machine-readable output).
```
